item.title: A message from Write to Right:
item.description: Hey STA! On December 10th, our school will join millions of people around the world for Amnesty International's Write for Rights campaign. This global event encourages people to write letters for individuals whose human rights are being violated. Together our letters can pressure governments to release prisoners, protect activists, and change unjust laws. This year, Owen Chow from Hong Kong is one of many people who we are helping. He stood up for democracy, despite the risk in his country. At the early age of 15, he dedicated his life to serve the underprivileged and build a fairer society. Owen was arrested in 2021 and sentenced to more than 12 years in prison. Let's help call on Hong Kong authorities to immediately release Owen. Keep an eye out for posters around the school to learn how you can take part and help make a difference.

item.title: A message from Mrs. Longval:
item.description: Good morning, STA! What an incredible day we had yesterday! Mrs. Longval would like to take a few moments to thank everyone who helped make our 2026 Movember Dodgeball Tournament such a huge success! First, a very special thank you to Mr. Longval, the person Mrs. Longval can always count on, no matter what the job requires! Whether it's setting up, organizing, refereeing or jumping in wherever help is needed, he's always there to lend a hand! A huge thank you to Mr. Benoit for taking the lead with our Grades 7 and 8 tournament! From organizing teams to putting on the referee stripes and keeping the games running, his efforts were greatly appreciated! Our intermediate students registered an impressive 14 teams this year! Thank you to all our Grades 7 and 8 students for your enthusiasm, participation and support of Movember, and to Mr. Benoit for helping spearhead our fundraising efforts at the intermediate level! At the Grades 9–12 level, a BIG congratulations to our 2026 Movember Dodgeball Champions, the HURT-U-BEES! What a great championship game! The afternoon was filled with friendly competition, great sportsmanship, teamwork, plenty of laughs and LOTS of physical activity! It was wonderful to see students coming together, supporting one another and having fun, all while raising awareness for such an important cause. Mrs. Longval would also like to give a special thank you to our Guidance Administrative Assistants, Ms. Marcellus and Mrs. Oldford, for their patience and support with our constantly changing team rosters and attendance lists! Your help behind the scenes was so appreciated! And of course, a VERY special thank you to our amazing student volunteers and tournament helpers! Liv, Sophie, Hailey, Paige, Nevaeh, Leah, Grace, Hanne and Yaya, THANK YOU! From judging and scorekeeping to setting up, cleaning up and keeping the tournament organized, you were absolutely fantastic! Mrs. Longval truly could not have pulled off such a successful day without your help. It's students like you, who are willing to step up, volunteer their time and help make things happen, who make STA such a great school community! And finally, thank you to every student and staff member who participated, contributed or supported this year's Movember initiative. While dodgeball was certainly the highlight of the day, the real reason behind this tournament was to bring attention to men's health, especially the importance of mental health, checking in on one another and encouraging conversations that matter. We haven't quite finished tallying our fundraising total yet, but once everything is counted, Mrs. Longval will share our final contribution to the Movember Canada Foundation on social media! Stay tuned for some great photos and videos from our awesome day! One last reminder: All students and staff can continue making donations through SchoolCash Online until Monday, November 30, the final day of Movember. Every dollar counts! Thank you again, STA, for helping keep this wonderful tradition alive and for showing that a little friendly competition can make a difference! Have a fantastic day, everyone!
